objective: 0.3.0 12/12: Support both local (per-project) and global (per-user) installations of HolyAgent in Claude Code and in pi, with a user-level HolyAgent config, and document that HolyAgent works in claude.ai chat and Cowork.
requirements: Maintainer (verbatim): "for 0.3.0, we will support both local and global installations for holyagent in claude and pi" and "also document that holyagent in claude chat/cowork (they're now unified) works correctly". The maintainer implements 0.3.0; this Intent records the plan.

Maintainer, 2026-11-07: implement 0.3.0 now, every part except the dropped auto-mode gate (pi 8/10); test with unit tests and recorded or synthesized fixtures only, no live Kimi runs; merge each PR once it is reviewed and green.

Facts (research assignment-0mw6rgzw5-cgu7): Claude Code installs plugins at user, project or local scope (enabledPlugins in ~/.claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json; local over project over user); a committed project entry enables but does not download, so each collaborator runs `claude plugin install --scope project` once; managed settings also exist. pi installs globally with `pi install` (~/.pi/agent/settings.json) or per project with `pi install -l` (.pi/settings.json); project settings override global ones, and project packages load only after project trust (print, JSON and RPC modes need --approve or defaultProjectTrust "always").

Claude Code: install, setup, doctor and the session-start setup check work the same at user, project and local scope; setup and doctor default to the scope the plugin is installed at, and the docs give the commands for each scope, including how a team shares a project-scope install.

pi: global and project-local installs both work; the docs present both, global first (root default); a project-local install documents the trust step, and specialists of a project-local install inherit the parent session's project trust (--approve only when the parent trusted the project; root default). The behavior when HolyAgent is declared at both scopes is verified during implementation.

User config (maintainer: "Add ~/.holyagent config"): a user-level ~/.holyagent/config.json with the same Effect Schema as .holyagent/config.json (common settings, pi section, claude section) holds per-user defaults; a project's .holyagent/config.json overrides it key by key; both are decoded with onExcessProperty error before merging.

claude.ai chat and Cowork (one Claude since 2026-09-16): plugins install per account from Customize > Plugins (no local or global notion there; an organization Owner can set a plugin to Installed by default or Required). The docs state, as tested by the maintainer, that HolyAgent works correctly there, replacing the earlier statement in docs/usage.md and docs/requirements.md that it does not work because of how hooks are activated; plain chat still loads skills only.
Tests cover install scope resolution for setup and doctor and the user/project config merge inside the existing CI jobs.

Decided (maintainer): for security-relevant pi features (computer use, T3 device access, the web tools), a false in the user-level ~/.holyagent/config.json is final: a project config can turn them off but cannot turn them back on. Every other key keeps the project-wins merge. Setup does not write T3's context meter, and the config has no key for it (maintainer: "don't set it").

Decided (maintainer, 2026-11-09: "both should default to user btw, but option 1", then "User for both"): bare holyagent setup and doctor infer their scope only from the user's own files: an enabled entry in the uncommitted .claude/settings.local.json makes both the Claude Code and the Pi steps local, else user. A committed .claude/settings.json that enables the plugin never moves either off user scope; setup prints a line that the repository enables it and that --scope project targets it. An explicit --scope always wins. Reason: a cloned repository must not choose where setup writes or which registry a Pi install uses.

Found (research assignment-0mw8td52p-27ab): Pi specialists run in-process as AgentSessions of @tintinweb/pi-subagents, so they share the root process and its resolved project trust; there is no child pi command line and no --approve to pass. The docs (docs/pi/approval.md, docs/pi/installation.md) say so, and setup or doctor tells a project-local install under RPC mode (T3) that an unknown project resolves untrusted without a prompt unless defaultProjectTrust or a stored trust decision allows it.
